questions.question: Accordioning to the Indian Government how many Khelo India State Centres of Excellence (KISCEs) were notified by the Government of India as of June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**34**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of **June 2025**, the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** has notified a total of **34** **Khelo India State Centres of Excellence** (**KISCEs**) across **31 States and Union Territories** in **India**.
 
• The **KISCE** initiative is a flagship program under the **Khelo India Scheme**, aimed at upgrading existing sports infrastructure in **States** and **Union Territories** to a world-class standard.
 
• Each center is tasked with focusing on specific **Olympic sport disciplines** to ensure concentrated development of talent and resources, helping **India** improve its standing in the **Olympic Games**.
 
• The selection of these **34** centers is based on the quality of existing infrastructure, coaching facilities, and the performance history of the **State** in particular sports.
 
• Financial assistance is provided by the **Central Government** to these centers to cover recurring and non-recurring costs, including **sports science** support, high-performance coaches, and technical equipment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Khelo India Scheme**:
 
 
• Launched in the financial year **2017-18**, this umbrella scheme was introduced by the **Government of India** to revive the sports culture at the grassroots level.
 
• The scheme is divided into **12 verticals**, ranging from infrastructure development to talent identification and community coaching.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Objectives**:
 
 
• The primary goal of **KISCE** is to create a robust ecosystem for athletes who have moved past the introductory stage and are ready for high-performance training.
 
• By **June 2025**, the integration of **sports science** (including nutrition, physiotherapy, and psychology) has become a mandatory component of these centers to ensure the holistic development of athletes.
 
 
 
• **Identification of Talent**:
 
 
• Athletes for these centers are often identified through national competitions such as the **Khelo India Youth Games** and **Khelo India University Games**.
 
• Selected athletes receive a **scholarship** and access to **residential training facilities**, aiming for peak performance in the **2028** and **2032** **Olympic Games**.
 
 
 
• **Role of States and UTs**:
 
 
• While the **Central Government** provides the funding and technical guidelines, the day-to-day management of these **34** centers remains with the respective **State Governments** or **UT Administrations**.
 
• This collaborative model ensures that the development of sports is not centralized but spread across the diverse geography of **India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The number of **KISCEs** has seen a steady increase since the first batch was announced, reflecting the government's commitment to reaching a target of at least one center of excellence in every **State** and **UT**.
 
• The **Sports Authority of India** (**SAI**) acts as the monitoring agency for these centers, ensuring that the quality of training meets international benchmarks.
 
• Prominent sports included in the **KISCE** focus list are **Archery**, **Athletics**, **Boxing**, **Hockey**, **Shooting**, and **Weightlifting**.
</ul

questions.question: How many cities were covered under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) by June 2025 to combat air pollution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**131**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** is a long-term, time-bound, national-level strategy to tackle the air pollution problem across India in a comprehensive manner.
 
• By **June 2025**, the total number of cities covered under this flagship program is **131**.
 
• These cities are primarily identified as **non-attainment cities**, which means they did not meet the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)** for five consecutive years.
 
• The program initially started with **102 cities** in **2019**, which was later expanded to **122**, and eventually to **131** cities to include those receiving grants under the **XV Finance Commission** for million-plus population cities.
 
• The primary objective of covering these **131 cities** is to implement city-specific action plans to reduce the levels of **Particulate Matter (PM10 and PM2.5)** significantly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Launch and Governance:**
 
 
• The **NCAP** was launched in **January 2019** by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**.
 
• It represents the first such effort in **India** to frame a national framework for air quality management with a time-bound reduction target.
 
 
 
• **Revised Targets:**
 
 
• Initially, the goal was to achieve a **20% to 30% reduction** in particulate matter concentration by **2024** (with **2017** as the base year).
 
• In **September 2022**, the Government of India updated the goal to a **40% reduction** in particulate matter levels or achieving the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards** by **2025-26**.
 
 
 
• **PRANA Portal:**
 
 
• To monitor the progress of the program in these **131 cities**, the government launched **PRANA (Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities)**.
 
• This portal tracks the physical and financial status of city action plan implementation and disseminates information on air quality to the public.
 
 
 
• **Funding Mechanisms:**
 
 
• Funding for the program is funneled through the **Control of Pollution** scheme for **82 cities** with a population below one million.
 
• For the remaining **49 cities** (million-plus cities), funding is provided through the **XV Finance Commission** air quality grants.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Multi-Sectoral Approach:** The **NCAP** focuses on various sources of pollution, including **industrial emissions**, **vehicular exhaust**, **biomass burning**, and **construction dust**.
 
• **Institutional Framework:** It involves collaboration between the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)**, and **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)** to ensure ground-level execution of clean air plans.
 
• **Monitoring Stations:** As part of the program, there has been a significant increase in the number of **Manual Monitoring Stations** and **Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS)** across the **131 identified cities** to provide real-time data.
 
• **Base Year:** The base year for measuring the concentration of pollutants and calculating the percentage of reduction is **2017**.
</ul

questions.question: What was the revised International Poverty Line (IPL) set by the World Bank for India in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**$3.00/day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In **June 2025**, the **World Bank** officially updated the **International Poverty Line (IPL)** to **$3.00 per day**, a significant increase from the previous standard of **$2.15 per day** established in **2022**.
 
• This revision is based on the latest **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** data, which accounts for changes in the global **cost of living** and **inflation** rates across different nations.
 
• For **India**, this update is particularly relevant as it serves as a benchmark for international organizations to assess the progress of **poverty alleviation** programs and economic growth.
 
• The **$3.00/day** threshold is used to define **extreme poverty** globally, ensuring that the metric reflects the minimum cost for basic food, clothing, and shelter in the current economic climate of **2025**.

questions.question: When was the International Day of Families observed in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**May 15**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Day of Families** is observed annually on **May 15**. In the year **2025**, this observance continues its tradition of highlighting the importance of the family unit in the global community.
 
• The day was officially proclaimed by the **United Nations General Assembly** in **1993** under resolution **A/RES/47/237**. It reflects the significance that the international community attaches to families as basic units of society.
 
• The first official observance took place in **1994**, which was also designated as the **International Year of the Family**. This initiative aims to promote awareness of issues relating to families and to increase knowledge of the social, economic, and demographic processes affecting them.
 
• Each year, the **United Nations** selects a specific theme for the day. These themes often focus on **education**, **poverty alleviation**, **work-family balance**, and **social integration** to strengthen family-centered policies.
 
• The **2025** observance serves as a platform for policy-makers and non-governmental organizations to discuss **demographic trends**, such as **aging populations** and **migration**, and their specific impacts on family structures worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Day of Parents (June 1):**
 
 
• Proclaimed by the **UN General Assembly** in **2012**, this day is observed on **June 1** to honor parents throughout the world for their selfless commitment to children. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **World Population Day (July 11):**
 
 
• Observed on **July 11**, this day seeks to focus attention on the urgency and importance of population issues. It was established by the **Governing Council of the United Nations Development Programme** in **1989**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• Families play a crucial role in achieving the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development**. Objectives such as **Goal 1 (No Poverty)**, **Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-being)**, and **Goal 4 (Quality Education)** are heavily dependent on stable family environments and supportive **government policies**.
 
 
 
• **Demographic Shifts:**
 
 
• Recent data from the **United Nations** suggests that family sizes are shrinking globally, and the number of **single-parent households** is rising. The **International Day of Families** encourages **member states** to adapt their legal and social frameworks to these evolving dynamics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **May 15** date remains constant every year, regardless of the day of the week. In **2025**, the International Day of Families falls on a **Thursday**.
 
• The **Division for Inclusive Social Development (DISD)**, part of the **UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)**, is the primary body responsible for organizing activities and research related to this day.
 
• Governments often use this day to launch **social security schemes**, **parental leave benefits**, and **childcare initiatives** to support the **well-being** of their citizens.
</ul

questions.question: On 26 August 2025, a deadly landslide near which pilgrimage site in Reasi district, Jammu & Kashmir, killed dozens and triggered a high-level investigation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vaishno Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tragic landslide occurred on **26 August 2025** near the world-famous **Vaishno Devi** shrine, which is located in the **Reasi district** of the Union Territory of **Jammu & Kashmir**.
 
• The incident took place on the track leading to the holy cave, specifically affecting the **Himkoti route** or the traditional **Bhavan-Sanjichhat** stretch, causing several casualties and leading to a **high-level investigation** ordered by the administration.
 
• The **Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board (SMVDSB)**, which manages the pilgrimage, immediately suspended the **Yatra** for safety reasons and launched a massive rescue operation involving the **NDRF**, **SDRF**, and local police.
 
• Preliminary reports suggested that the landslide was triggered by heavy rainfall in the **Trikuta Hills**, highlighting the geological vulnerability of the **Himalayan** region during the monsoon and post-monsoon periods.
 
• The **Lieutenant Governor** of **Jammu & Kashmir**, who serves as the Chairman of the **Shrine Board**, announced a committee to probe the causes of the slide and to review the **disaster management** protocols in place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vaishno Devi Temple:**
 
 
• Located at an altitude of approximately **5,200 feet**, the shrine is situated in the **Trikuta Mountains** near **Katra**.
 
• It is one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in **India**, attracting millions of devotees annually. The base camp for the trek is **Katra**, located in the **Reasi district**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context of Reasi:**
 
 
• The **Reasi district** is home to significant landmarks including the **Chenab Bridge**, the world’s highest railway bridge, and the **Shiv Khori** cave.
 
• The region is characterized by steep slopes and sedimentary rock formations, making it susceptible to **landslides** and **soil erosion** during intense weather events.
 
 
 
• **Other Pilgrimage Sites Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Amarnath Cave:** Located in the **Anantnag** district of **Jammu & Kashmir** at a much higher altitude of **12,756 feet**. It is famous for the natural **Ice Lingam**.
 
• **Hemkund Sahib:** A prominent **Sikh** pilgrimage site located in the **Chamoli district** of **Uttarakhand**, dedicated to **Guru Gobind Singh**.
 
• **Shankaracharya Temple:** An ancient temple dedicated to **Lord Shiva** located on the **Gopadari Hill** in **Srinagar**, **Jammu & Kashmir**.
 
 
 
• **Safety and Mitigation Measures:**
 
 
• The **SMVDSB** has previously installed **wire mesh** and **retaining walls** along the track to prevent falling stones.
 
• Advanced **Weather Forecasting** systems and **CCTV monitoring** are used to track real-time conditions on the **13 km** trek from **Katra** to the **Bhavan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Disaster Response:** The **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** is the specialized body constituted under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, to deal with such emergencies in **India**.
 
• **Investigation Scope:** The **high-level investigation** typically involves geologists from the **Geological Survey of India (GSI)** to study the stability of the slopes and recommend long-term safety measures like **slope stabilization** and **tunneling**.
 
• **Impact on Pilgrimage:** The **Vaishno Devi Yatra** is a major economic driver for the **Union Territory**, supporting thousands of livelihoods in **Katra** and surrounding areas; hence, safety is a top priority for the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.

questions.question: Which team won the 2025 UEFA-Champions League?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Paris Saint‑Germain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paris Saint-Germain (PSG)** emerged as the champions of the **2024-25 UEFA Champions League**, marking a historic achievement for the club.
 
• The final match was held on **May 31, 2025**, at the iconic **Allianz Arena** in **Munich**, **Germany**.
 
• This victory represents **PSG's** first-ever **European Cup/UEFA Champions League** title, fulfilling a long-standing ambition for the **Paris**-based side.
 
• By winning this title, **PSG** became the second **French club** in history to win the prestigious trophy, following **Olympique de Marseille's** victory in **1993**.
 
• The **2025** final was the grand finale of the **70th season** of Europe's premier club football tournament and the **33rd season** since it was renamed the **UEFA Champions League**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **New Tournament Format:**
 
 
• The **2024–25** season introduced a revolutionary **"Swiss-style"** format, expanding the number of participating teams from **32 to 36**.
 
• In this new **League Phase**, each team played **eight matches** against eight different opponents (four at home and four away) instead of the traditional group stage.
 
• This format change aimed to increase the number of high-profile matches early in the competition and provided more revenue opportunities for the **UEFA** member associations.
 
 
 
• **Venue Details:**
 
 
• The **Allianz Arena**, home to **Bayern Munich**, hosted its second **Champions League** final in **2025**; the first was the famous **2012** "Finale dahoam."
 
• The stadium has a seating capacity of approximately **75,000** for domestic matches and around **67,000** for international **UEFA** events.
 
 
 
• **Managerial Success:**
 
 
• The team was led by head coach **Luis Enrique**, who had previously won the tournament with **Barcelona** in **2015**.
 
• His tactical approach emphasized **possession-based football** and high-intensity pressing, which proved decisive throughout the **knockout stages**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Qualification and Rewards:**
 
 
• As the winners of the **2025 UEFA Champions League**, **PSG** automatically qualified for the **2025–26 UEFA Champions League** league stage.
 
• They also earned the right to play against the winners of the **2024–25 UEFA Europa League** in the **2025 UEFA Super Cup**.
 
• Furthermore, the victory ensured their participation in the expanded **2025 FIFA Club World Cup** scheduled to be held in the **United States**.
 
 
 
• **Financial Impact:**
 
 
• The winner of the tournament received a base prize of **€20 million** for the final victory, in addition to accumulated bonuses from earlier rounds, totaling over **€100 million** in overall revenue.
 
• The **UEFA Champions League** remains the most lucrative club competition in world sports, with total distributions exceeding **€2.4 billion** for the **2024-25** cycle.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The **2025** season marked a shift in European football hierarchy, as **PSG** overcame perennial giants like **Real Madrid** and **Manchester City** during their path to the trophy.
 
• Key players such as **Ousmane Dembélé**, **Vitinha**, and **Bradley Barcola** played pivotal roles in the club's successful campaign.

questions.question: Which day in February 2025 was celebrated as the National Science Day in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**28 February**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Science Day** is celebrated in India every year on **28 February** to commemorate the discovery of the **Raman Effect**.
 
• On this day in **1928**, the renowned Indian physicist **Sir Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman** (C.V. Raman) announced the discovery of the **scattering of light**, which was later named after him as the **Raman Effect**.
 
• For his revolutionary work in the field of **physics**, **Sir C.V. Raman** was honored with the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1930**. He was the first **Indian** and first **Asian** to receive a Nobel Prize in any branch of **science**.
 
• In **1986**, the **National Council for Science and Technology Communication (NCSTC)** requested the **Government of India** to designate **February 28** as National Science Day.
 
• The first National Science Day was celebrated on **February 28, 1987**, with the aim of spreading the message of the importance of **scientific applications** in the daily lives of the people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sir C.V. Raman:**
 
 
• He was born on **7 November 1888** in **Tiruchirapalli**, **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• Apart from the Nobel Prize, he was also awarded India's highest civilian honor, the **Bharat Ratna**, in **1954**.
 
• He was also a recipient of the **Lenin Peace Prize** in **1957**.
 
 
 
• **The Raman Effect:**
 
 
• It is a phenomenon in **spectroscopy** where a **photon** of light interacts with a molecule, leading to a change in the **wavelength** and energy of the light.
 
• This discovery is widely used in **chemical laboratories** to identify the structure of molecules and in **medical diagnostics**.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the Day:**
 
 
• To display all the activities, efforts, and achievements in the field of **science** for human welfare.
 
• To give an opportunity to the **scientific-minded** citizens in the **country** and encourage them to popularize **science and technology**.
 
• To foster a **scientific temper** among the youth of **India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Department of Science and Technology (DST)** acts as a nodal agency to support and coordinate the celebration of National Science Day throughout the **country**.
 
• The government announces a specific **theme** for National Science Day every year. For example, the theme for **2024** was "**Indigenous Technologies for Viksit Bharat**", focusing on homegrown **innovation**.
 
• Various awards, such as the **National Awards for Science Popularization**, are conferred on this day to individuals and **organizations** for their outstanding contribution to **science communication**.
 
• Developing a **scientific temper**, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform is a **Fundamental Duty** of Indian citizens under **Article 51A** of the **Constitution of India**.
</ul

questions.question: Which Swedish athlete won the Laureus Sportsman of the Year 2025 for his world record-breaking performances in pole vault?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mondo Duplantis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Armand "Mondo" Duplantis** is a **Swedish-American** athlete who competes for **Sweden** and is widely considered the greatest **pole vaulter** in the history of the sport.
 
• He is recognized for his extraordinary **world record-breaking performances**, having broken the world record multiple times throughout his career. In **April 2024**, he set a new world record of **6.24 meters** at the **Diamond League** meeting in **Xiamen**, **China**.
 
• The **Laureus World Sportsman of the Year** award is a prestigious global honor given to the male athlete who has demonstrated supreme athletic achievement. Duplantis has been a frequent nominee and winner in various categories due to his dominance in track and field.
 
• His accolades include winning the **Gold Medal** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** and securing titles at the **World Athletics Championships** in **2022** (Eugene) and **2023** (Budapest).
 
• His ability to consistently improve his own records by small increments (the **"Bubka"** method) has made him a standout figure in global sports, leading to his selection for the **2025** cycle honors based on his **2024** season performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Laureus World Sports Awards:**
 
 
• Established in **1999** by founding patrons **Daimler** and **Richemont**, these awards celebrate the highest sporting achievements of the year.
 
• The first ceremony was held in **2000** in **Monte Carlo**, with **Tiger Woods** winning the first Sportsman of the Year award.
 
• The winners are selected by the **Laureus World Sports Academy**, which consists of over **70 sporting legends**.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Athletes:**
 
 
• **Karsten Warholm**: A **Norwegian** athlete who holds the world record in the **400-meter hurdles** (**45.94 seconds**). He is a multiple-time **World Champion** and **Olympic Gold medalist**.
 
• **Jakob Ingebrigtsen**: A **Norwegian** middle-distance runner who won **Olympic Gold** in the **1500 meters** at the **Tokyo Games** and holds several world and European records in the **1500m**, **2000m**, and **5000m**.

questions.question: Who received the Vigyan Shri award in 2024 for his contributions to Agricultural Science?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Anandharamakrishnan C**__.

__
 
• **Dr. Anandharamakrishnan C** was honored with the **Vigyan Shri** award in **2024** for his outstanding contributions to the field of **Agricultural Science**.
 
• He currently serves as the **Director** of the **CSIR-National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (NIIST)**, located in **Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala**.
 
• His research work primarily focuses on **food processing**, **food engineering**, and the application of **nanotechnology** in the agricultural and food sectors.
 
• He is widely recognized for his pioneering work in **3D food printing**, **spray drying**, and **electrospraying** of food bioactive compounds to improve their bioavailability.
 
• The **Vigyan Shri** is one of the four categories of the **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar**, newly instituted by the **Government of India** to recognize distinguished contributions to **Science and Technology**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (2024):**
 
 
• The **Government of India** announced the first-ever **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar** in **2024**, replacing various previous science awards with a unified national framework.
 
• A total of **33 awards** were announced in **August 2024**, comprising **1 Vigyan Ratna**, **13 Vigyan Shri**, **18 Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar**, and **1 Vigyan Team** award.
 
• The awards were presented by the **President of India**, **Droupadi Murmu**, at **Rashtrapati Bhavan**.
 
 
 
• **Award Categories:**
 
 
• **Vigyan Ratna:** Awarded for lifetime achievements and contributions in any field of science and technology. In **2024**, it was awarded to **Prof. Govindarajan Padmanabhan** for his work in **Biological Sciences**.
 
• **Vigyan Shri:** Conferred for distinguished contributions to a specific field. Recipients in **2024** included **Prof. Jayant Bhalchandra Udgaonkar** (Biological Sciences) and **Dr. Avesh Kumar Tyagi** (Atomic Energy).
 
• **Vigyan Yuva–Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar:** Recognizes young scientists (up to **45 years** of age) for exceptional contributions.
 
• **Vigyan Team:** Given to a team of **3 or more** scientists for collaborative research work. In **2024**, this was awarded to the **ISRO Chandrayaan-3 Team**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Agricultural Science in RVP:**
 
 
• The inclusion of **Agricultural Science** as a dedicated category highlights the government's focus on **food security**, **sustainable farming**, and **agri-tech innovations**.
 
• **Dr. Anandharamakrishnan's** recognition emphasizes the importance of **value addition** in agricultural produce and the reduction of **post-harvest losses** through engineering interventions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar** is organized across **13 domains**, including **Physics**, **Chemistry**, **Biological Sciences**, **Mathematics & Computer Science**, **Earth Sciences**, **Medicine**, **Engineering Sciences**, **Agricultural Science**, **Environmental Science**, **Technology & Innovation**, **Atomic Energy**, **Space Science & Technology**, and others.
 
• The selection process is governed by the **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar Committee (RVPC)**, headed by the **Principal Scientific Adviser** to the Government of India.
 
• Recipients of the **Vigyan Shri** award receive a **Sanad** (certificate) and a **Medallion**, but no monetary cash prize is associated with these specific national honors, focusing instead on the prestige of the recognition.

questions.question: Who among the following participated in the Outreach Session of the G7 Summit in Canada in June 2025?

• Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** participated in the **Outreach Session** of the **51st G7 Summit**, which was held in **Canada** in **June 2025**.
 
• India was invited as an **Outreach Country**, continuing its streak of participation in the G7 meetings as a key global partner and a representative of the **Global South**.
 
• During the summit, the Indian Prime Minister engaged in discussions regarding **global governance**, **artificial intelligence**, **energy security**, and **sustainable development**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **51st G7 Summit** saw the participation of leaders from the seven member nations and invited heads from various international organizations and partner countries to address **geopolitical tensions** and **economic stability**.
 
• The invitation to **Narendra Modi** reflects India's growing influence in the international arena and its strategic partnership with G7 nations like the **United States**, **France**, and **Canada**.

__
 
• **The Group of Seven (G7):**
 
 
• The **G7** is an intergovernmental political forum consisting of seven of the world's advanced economies: **Canada**, **France**, **Germany**, **Italy**, **Japan**, the **United Kingdom**, and the **United States**.
 
• The **European Union (EU)** is also represented at the G7, though it is not a formal member.
 
• The group was established in **1975** (initially as the G6) to provide a platform for industrialized nations to coordinate **economic policies** and tackle global crises.
 
 
 
• **G7 Presidency and Hosting:**
 
 
• The presidency of the G7 rotates annually among its members. **Canada** held the presidency for the year **2025** and hosted the summit.
 
• The previous summit, the **50th G7 Summit**, was hosted by **Italy** in **June 2024** at **Borgo Egnazia** (Puglia).
 
• India has been a regular invitee to the G7 summits since **2019**, when it was invited by **France** for the **Biarritz Summit**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Outreach Session:**
 
 
• The **Outreach Session** is a special segment of the G7 summit where leaders from non-member nations and international organizations are invited to discuss specific global issues like **climate change**, **health**, and **digital transformation**.
 
• It serves as a bridge between the **G7** and the rest of the world, particularly the **developing nations**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's Role:** India often uses the G7 platform to advocate for the concerns of the **Global South**, emphasizing **inclusive growth** and **technological equity**.
 
• **Other Options:** While **Amit Shah** (Union Home Minister), **Nirmala Sitharaman** (Finance Minister), and **Droupadi Murmu** (President of India) hold high constitutional and cabinet positions, it is traditionally the **Prime Minister** who represents India at G7 Outreach summits.
 
• **Historical Context:** India's first participation in a G7 (then G8) summit was in **2003** under the leadership of then PM **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**.
 
• **Key Themes:** The **2025 Summit** in **Canada** emphasized **clean energy transitions** and **supply chain resilience** in the face of shifting global dynamics.
</ul

• The agreement focuses on enhancing **joint military exercises**, sharing **intelligence**, and collaborating on **counter-terrorism** operations to address evolving regional security challenges.
 
• A major component of this pact involves **Defense Industrial Cooperation**, where both nations agreed to explore joint ventures in **defense production** and the transfer of **military technology**.

• **Humanitarian and Peacekeeping:** Beyond combat operations, the pact includes provisions for **disaster management** and cooperation in **United Nations Peacekeeping** missions where both countries are active contributors.

questions.question: Which regulatory provisions did the the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) reference while imposing the fine on Acko General Insurance for violations related to outsourcing and commissions in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Section 40(1) of Insurance Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** took regulatory action against **Acko General Insurance** in **May 2025** for violations concerning **outsourcing** and **commission** payments.
 
• **Section 40(1)** of the **Insurance Act, 1938** serves as a critical provision that prohibits the payment of **remuneration** or **reward** by way of **commission** to any person for soliciting or procuring insurance business in **India**, unless that person is an authorized **insurance agent** or an **insurance intermediary**.
 
• The investigation by **IRDAI** revealed that the insurer had entered into arrangements that resulted in payments exceeding the permissible **commission caps** or were directed toward entities not eligible under the regulatory framework.
 
• The fine was imposed because the **outsourcing** expenses were found to be a means of circumventing the statutory limits on **acquisition costs** and **expenses of management**. *Hence, the statement regarding Section 40(1) is correct.*
 
• This regulatory intervention emphasizes the necessity for **general insurance companies** to adhere strictly to the **Insurance Act** and **IRDAI regulations** to maintain market integrity and protect **policyholders'** interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI):**
 
 
• It is a **statutory body** formed under the **IRDAI Act, 1999**.
 
• The **headquarters** of the authority are located in **Hyderabad**, having moved from **New Delhi** in **2001**.
 
• Its primary mission is to regulate and promote the **insurance** and **reinsurance** industries in **India** while ensuring the **financial security** of the sector.
 
 
 
• **The Insurance Act, 1938:**
 
 
• This is the **foundational legislation** governing the insurance sector in **India**.
 
• It provides the **legal framework** for the **registration** of insurance companies, **investment** of assets, and the **prohibition** of rebates and unauthorized commissions.
 
• **Section 64V** of this Act specifically deals with the **assets and liabilities** of an insurer and the determination of the **solvency margin**.
 
 
 
• **Outsourcing Regulations:**
 
 
• Under the **IRDAI (Outsourcing of Activities by Indian Insurers) Regulations, 2017**, insurers are strictly prohibited from outsourcing **core functions** such as **underwriting**, **claims settlement**, and **compliance** functions.
 
• The regulations aim to ensure that insurers retain **effective control** over their operations and do not utilize outsourcing as a loophole to pay extra **commissions**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Section 40(1) Enforcement:** The enforcement of this section ensures that the **cost of insurance** does not escalate due to unregulated **payouts** to intermediaries, which ultimately benefits the **end consumer**.
 
• **Compliance Framework:** Every insurer must submit an **annual certificate** signed by the **CEO** and **Compliance Officer**, affirming that all **outsourcing** arrangements and **commission** payments are in line with the **statutory provisions**.
 
• **Penalties:** **IRDAI** has the power to impose **monetary penalties** ranging from **1 lakh** to **1 crore** rupees per day of continuing violation or cancel the **certificate of registration** under extreme circumstances.
</ul

questions.question: In November 2025, the standing committee of the National Board for Wildlife approved a proposal to construct a Pinjoli bridge in which of the following wildlife sanctuaries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Standing Committee** of the **National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)**, in its meeting held in **November 2025**, cleared the proposal for the construction of the **Pinjoli bridge**.
 
• The bridge is located within the **Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary**, situated in the **West Kameng** district of **Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
• This infrastructure project is a critical component of the **Bhalukpong-Charduar-Tawang (BCT) road**, which is of **strategic importance** for the movement of **defense forces** and logistics toward the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**.
 
• The **Pinjoli bridge** construction involves the diversion of forest land, and the approval was granted with specific **mitigation measures** to ensure the protection of the local **flora and fauna**.
 
• The **NBWL** is the apex body in India for all wildlife-related matters and its approval is mandatory for any project passing through **protected areas** like **national parks** and **sanctuaries**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary:**
 
 
• Located in **Arunachal Pradesh**, it covers an area of approximately **218 square kilometers**.
 
• It gained international fame in **2006** following the discovery of a rare bird species named **Bugun Liocichla**.
 
• The sanctuary is part of the **Kameng Elephant Reserve** and is known for its incredible **altitudinal range**, varying from **500 meters** to **3,250 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Dehing Patkai Wildlife Sanctuary:**
 
 
• Located in the **Dibrugarh** and **Tinsukia** districts of **Assam**, it is often referred to as the **"Amazon of the East"**.
 
• It was officially declared a **National Park** in **June 2021**. It is the only sanctuary in India that is home to **seven different species of wild cats**.
 
 
 
• **Sepahijala Wildlife Sanctuary:**
 
 
• This sanctuary is located in **Tripura** and is famous for its **Clouded Leopard National Park**.
 
• It is a prominent site for the conservation of the **Phayre's leaf monkey** (also known as the **Spectacled Monkey**), which is the state animal of **Tripura**.
 
 
 
• **Dzukou Valley Wildlife Sanctuary:**
 
 
• Situated at the border of **Nagaland** and **Manipur**, it is renowned for its **natural beauty** and seasonal blooms of the **Dzukou Lily**.
 
• The valley is a popular **trekking destination** and faces ecological threats from **forest fires** and unregulated tourism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Board for Wildlife (NBWL):** It is a **statutory body** constituted under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**. The **Prime Minister** serves as the **ex-officio chairman** of the board.
 
• **Border Roads Organization (BRO):** Most strategic bridges in this region, including those near **Eaglenest**, are executed by the **BRO** under **Project Vartak** to enhance **national security** infrastructure.
 
• **Wildlife Clearances:** Any non-forestry activity within a **protected area** requires a recommendation from the **Standing Committee** of the **NBWL** after initial scrutiny by the **State Board for Wildlife**.
</ul

questions.question: On 28 October 2025, the Union Cabinet approved the Terms of Reference for which commission responsible for recommending salaries and retirement benefits for central government employees?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8th Central Pay Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet** of India officially approved the **Terms of Reference (ToR)** for the **8th Central Pay Commission** on **28 October 2025**.
 
• The primary mandate of the **8th Central Pay Commission** is to review, examine, and recommend changes to the existing **salary structure**, **allowances**, and **retirement benefits** for all **Central Government employees**, including the **Armed Forces** and **pensioners**.
 
• The recommendations are expected to benefit approximately **48 lakh active employees** and over **67 lakh pensioners** across the country, aiming to address the rising cost of living and inflation.
 
• As per the standard decadal cycle followed by the government, the implementation of the new pay structure recommended by the **8th Pay Commission** is likely to take effect from **January 1, 2026**.
 
• The commission is tasked with evolving a comprehensive framework that balances the financial needs of the employees with the **fiscal health** of the **Government of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:** The first Pay Commission in India was established in **1946**, chaired by **Srinivasa Varadachariar**. Since then, the government has traditionally constituted a new commission every **10 years** to revise the pay scales.
 
• **The 7th Central Pay Commission:** It was set up in **February 2014** under the chairmanship of **Justice Ashok Kumar Mathur**. Its recommendations were implemented with effect from **January 1, 2016**, introducing a **Fitment Factor** of **2.57** for basic pay calculation.
 
• **Composition of the Commission:** A typical Pay Commission is headed by a **Chairperson**, usually a retired **Judge of the Supreme Court** or a **High Court**, and includes **full-time members**, a **Member-Secretary**, and part-time members with expertise in economics and administration.
 
• **Purpose and Objective:** The commissions focus on ensuring that government compensation remains competitive and fair, taking into account the **Consumer Price Index (Industrial Workers)** and the general economic environment of the **nation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fitment Factor:** This is a crucial numerical value used to arrive at the new basic pay. For the **8th Pay Commission**, there is significant speculation and demand for an increased fitment factor to boost the **minimum wage**.
 
• **Scope of Coverage:** The recommendations of the **Pay Commission** apply to **Central Government** employees, **All India Services**, personnel of **Union Territories**, and the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department**.
 
• **Fiscal Impact:** The implementation of such commissions usually results in a significant increase in **government expenditure**, which is a major factor in the **Union Budget** planning and the management of the **fiscal deficit**.
 
• **Terms of Reference (ToR):** This document outlines the specific guidelines, limitations, and areas of study for the commission, serving as the **legal and administrative roadmap** for its functioning.
</ul
